- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2% correction in the direction of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; cap forecast at 1–2% below true mean of recent 10–15 day range.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model tends to underperform; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for hidden volatility or policy surprises.
